title: Titan rejects top_p=0 with a 422 before calling Bedrock
answers: Titan top_p must be greater than 0
422 for top_p zero on amazon titan
why does top_p=0 fail for Titan but work for other models
body:
Invariant: Titan requires topP strictly greater than 0, but MLflow accepts top_p=0. AWSTitanAdapter.completions_to_model raises AIGatewayException with status 422 when payload top_p == 0, before any request is built.
Enforced by: the top_p == 0 check in mlflow/gateway/providers/bedrock.py:AWSTitanAdapter.completions_to_model, placed next to the existing 422 for n != 1.
What breaks if skipped: the request goes to Bedrock with a value Titan rejects, so the caller gets a backend validation failure rather than a clear gateway error.
Test: tests/gateway/providers/test_bedrock.py:test_bedrock_titan_rejects_top_p_zero asserts the 422 and that _request is never called. Keep Jurassic unaffected; this check is Titan-only.
applies: Titan model requests through the Bedrock gateway provider; the check is Titan-only and does not apply to AI21 Jurassic.
says: Setting top p to zero on Amazon Titan models returns an unprocessable entity error.
Why does setting sampling probability to zero fail on Amazon Titan through the gateway?
Amazon Titan requests through the gateway fail validation immediately when top p is zero.
Return a clear gateway validation error instead of backend provider failure when top p is zero.
search: The Bedrock gateway provider adapter for Amazon Titan rejects requests with top_p=0 with an AIGatewayException 422 before calling Bedrock. This invariant is enforced in mlflow/gateway/providers/bedrock.py:AWSTitanAdapter.completions_to_model next to the n != 1 check to prevent backend Bedrock validation failures. Tested in tests/gateway/providers/test_bedrock.py:test_bedrock_titan_rejects_top_p_zero to assert status 422 and that _request is never called. This check applies exclusively to Titan model requests and must keep AI21 Jurassic unaffected.
